dedupe_keys.name: iowa flood depth loss of function and restoration time for essential facilities

description: This case study assesses how floods would affect nine types of essential facilities in Iowa, such as hospitals, fire stations, police stations and schools. The authors, researchers at the University of Iowa, King Saud University and Giresun University, analysed six counties for flood depth, damage, loss of functionality and restoration time, and mapped facilities statewide against the 100-year and 500-year flood zones; the work is published as an open-access journal article. Coverage is the state of Iowa, with county-level detail. The article is free to read under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Caveats: results come from modelled flood scenarios and generic damage and restoration functions, not observed events. The study found that up to 39 percent of essential facilities lie within the flood extent, that in the 100-year scenario all but one of the six counties lost function in 100 percent of their facilities, and that most facilities would see 1 to 4 feet of water and restoration times of about 480 days. Simulation uses: exposure and restoration parameters for emergency service continuity and recovery models under flooding. Related records: the FEMA National Flood Hazard Layer (data-fema-national-flood-hazard-layer) defines the flood zones and Hazus (platform-hazus) provides the kind of depth-damage and restoration functions used.
